title: Treating bedwetting in a child
what: Enuresis is when a child over 5 wets the bed while asleep. It is common, and it can be treated.
why: If a child over 5 often wakes up wet, or bedwetting started again after a dry period.
duration: the visit usually takes 20 to 40 minutes; treatment usually takes several months
tell_doctor: How often there are wet nights
If there is daytime wetting or constipation
How much and when your child drinks
If there was stress: a move, school, a divorce

prepare.title: Diary
prepare.text: For a few days, write down how much your child drinks, when they use the toilet, and which nights are wet. This helps the doctor a lot.

prepare.title: Tests
prepare.text: A urine test is usually needed, sometimes an ultrasound. Ask the clinic.

prepare.title: Talk
prepare.text: Explain to your child that you are going to the doctor to get help, not to be scolded.

steps: The doctor asks you and your child questions
The doctor looks at the diary and test results
The doctor explains the plan: a drinking schedule, a bedwetting alarm, or medicine
feel: Improvement is usually gradual, and setbacks happen. This is normal
after: Do not scold or punish your child. It does not help
Praise your child for dry nights
Keep the diary and show it to the doctor
Come back as the doctor plans

faq.q: Will it go away on its own?
faq.a: It often goes away with age, but treatment speeds it up and eases your child's stress. Decide together with the doctor.

faq.q: Should I wake my child at night?
faq.a: Waking a child on a schedule usually does not teach them to stay dry. The doctor will tell you what to do in your case.

reminders.text: Bedwetting visit tomorrow. Bring the toilet diary and your child's documents.
